profile_metadata.purpose: Profile of the two input data files (schema, samples, coverage, data-quality issues) for the ZHVI vs. unemployment cross-correlation pipeline.

datasets.path: Unemployment in America Per US State.csv
datasets.encoding: utf-8-sig (file starts with a UTF-8 BOM: first column name is '\ufeffFIPS Code')
column_names: Total Civilian Non-Institutional Population in State/Area
Total Civilian Labor Force in State/Area
Percent (%) of Labor Force Employed in State/Area
Percent (%) of Labor Force Unemployed in State/Area
datasets.structure: long format, one row per State/Area x Year x Month

schema.note: mostly 2-digit state FIPS but '037' (Los Angeles County) is 3-digit -> do NOT rely on FIPS width; join on name instead. Not a USPS abbreviation.

schema.role: state/area name -> must be mapped to 2-letter USPS code
schema.note: 53 distinct values = 50 states + District of Columbia + 2 non-state rows ('Los Angeles County', 'New York city') that must be dropped.
already zero-padded; month convention is the calendar month (no day given) -> anchor timestamps to day 1

schema.column: Total Civilian Non-Institutional Population in State/Area
Total Civilian Labor Force in State/Area
Percent (%) of Labor Force Employed in State/Area
Percent (%) of Labor Force Unemployed in State/Area
schema.role: PRIMARY TARGET: unemployment rate (percent) -> the 'unemployment rate' series
schema.note: requires strip() then pd.to_numeric; 53 rows hold the en-dash placeholder '–' (missing) and all of them are in Year 2025 (future months) - none inside 2010-01..2019-12.

coverage.months_per_state: 599 for every State/Area (complete monthly series, no gaps)

data_quality.encoding_issue: UTF-8 BOM present; use encoding='utf-8-sig' or the first column name carries a stray \ufeff prefix
data_quality.numeric_parsing_issue: all numeric columns are strings with thousands separators and trailing whitespace; the unemployment rate column only needs .str.strip() before to_numeric

datasets.structure: wide format: one row per state, one column per month (month-END date labels), plus 6 identifier/meta columns

date_columns.pattern: YYYY-MM-DD, always the last calendar day of the month

schema.role: row index artifact of the CSV export
schema.note: 0..50, redundant with SizeRank; should be dropped

schema.role: state name (e.g. 'California', 'District of Columbia'); 51 distinct -> alternative join key against the unemployment 'State/Area' column
constant 'State' for all 51 rows (already state-level, no aggregation needed)
ALREADY a 2-letter USPS abbreviation (51 distinct, includes 'DC')
schema.note: use this as the state identifier for the ZHVI side; identical code set to the unemployment states after name->USPS mapping

schema.role: ZHVI (Zillow Home Value Index, USD) monthly values -> the 'home price index' series
schema.note: column labels are month-END dates and must be normalized to the first day of the same month

data_quality.note: 223 NaN cells exist across the full 1996-2020 history (early history of some smaller states) but none inside the 2010-01..2019-12 analysis window

joinability.state_identifier_normalization: Unemployment 'State/Area' (full names, incl. DC as 'District of Columbia') -> 2-letter USPS; Zillow 'StateName' is already USPS. A 50-states + DC name->USPS mapping resolves all rows.
joinability.timestamp_convention: both series anchored to the first day of the month: unemployment (Year '2010' + Month '01' -> 2010-01-01); ZHVI month-end labels ('2010-01-31' -> 2010-01-01). Both then share pd.date_range('2010-01-01','2019-12-01', freq='MS') = 120 periods.

readiness_checks_for_downstream.rolling_windows_fully_supported: ZHVI history starts 1996-01, unemployment starts 1976-01, so a 12-month rolling window with min_periods=6 is fully populated for every month of 2010-01..2019-12 (verified: 120/120 non-null months for all 51 states on both rolling-mean series)
readiness_checks_for_downstream.notes: With lag range -24..+24 on a 120-month index, each lag correlation uses the overlapping subset (>= 96 months), so estimates are well determined.

pitfalls_summary: Unemployment CSV has a UTF-8 BOM -> read with encoding='utf-8-sig'.
Unemployment numeric columns are strings with trailing spaces / thousands separators; the rate column needs strip() before to_numeric, and the placeholder '–' (en dash) becomes NaN.
Unemployment file mixes 2 non-state rows ('Los Angeles County', 'New York city') into State/Area -> drop them so only the 51 USPS states remain.
Unemployment 'FIPS Code' is not uniformly 2 chars ('037' for LA County) -> join on state name, not FIPS.
Zillow date columns are month-END labels; floor them to month start before joining to the unemployment month-start dates, otherwise the join yields zero matches.
Zillow uses 'DC' as StateName for 'District of Columbia'; the name->USPS map must include DC.
Zillow also contains 2020-01..2020-03 and history back to 1996-01; restrict/reindex to the fixed 2010-01..2019-12 index after computing rolling statistics.
